subject: MAP: Technical evaluation scoping and benchmark targets
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: MAP: Technical evaluation scoping and benchmark targets

Hi Aditi — thanks again for your time this morning. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps so we have the MAP milestone scoped for the technical evaluation. I attached an editable MAP (MediSync_MAP_v1.xlsx) and a blank benchmark template.

Summary of today's alignment
- Goal: Validate whether Redwood can meet MediSync's latency and cost targets for embedding and generation workloads powering the patient-authoring feature.
- Scope: end-to-end inference performance on the anonymized test set you agreed to share; model shortlist/hyperparameters; integration smoke test with 1k concurrent session simulation.

Proposed Technical Evaluation milestone (draft)
1) Test dataset delivery — owner: MediSync (Aditi) — dependency: anonymization + S3 access
2) Baseline run & orchestration — owner: Redwood (Marissa) — deliverable: benchmark CSV + logs
3) Latency & cost validation — owner: Redwood (Marissa) with support from Connor — success criteria below
4) Integration smoke test — owner: MediSync engineering — dependency: test environment creds
5) Go/no-go readout & decision — owners: MediSync + Redwood (Rishi to support commercial guardrails)

Benchmarks / success criteria (proposal)
- Latency: generation p95 <= 350ms for 512-token sequence (streaming enabled), p50 < 120ms.
- Throughput: sustained 120 qps steady-state across a 4-GPU dedicated pool for 512-token runs.
- Cost: inference token cost (model+infra) <= $0.0010 per generated token at target batch/kv-cache config.
- Quality: pass 90% of qualitative evaluation prompts (scoring rubric in sheet) and no critical hallucination failure modes on protected attributes.

Model shortlist (first-pass)
- Redwood-7B-v2-optimized (FP16 / q4) — low latency baseline
- Llama-2-13B-chat (int8/q4) — mid-range correctness vs cost
- Falcon-40B-instruct (ptq) — higher-quality candidate for content-heavy prompts
(we can expand the list after you share representative prompts)

Dependencies & blockers
- Procurement redlines (procurement@medisync.com) for test account access
- Access to the anonymized test set (S3 link + sample file)
- VPN or VPC peering for private deployment preview (if you want a full end-to-end run)

Next steps / asks
- Aditi: confirm target close window (you mentioned Nov 2026 end-of-month earlier) and provide S3 upload ETA
- Procurement: please review the sandbox access/NDAs and confirm by Nov 24 if possible
- Marissa: we'll need a prioritized prompt sheet and any long-tail token distribution guidance

I've attached the MAP draft and a benchmark template to make it easier to capture owners and acceptance criteria. If this looks right I'll lock the milestone dates into the MAP and follow up with a proposed test schedule.

Best,
Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Adding technical detail so the MAP's "Latency & cost validation" milestone is actionable from a benchmarking perspective. Suggested additions for the benchmark template and acceptance criteria:

Benchmark methodology (add to template):
- Workload: 3 prompt sets (short, medium, long) reflecting typical user flows; use requested sample prompts from MediSync.
- Sequence lengths: 64, 256, 512 tokens; streaming enabled for the 512 case.
- Measurement: p50/p95/p99 latency for token-generation (end-to-end from request to first useful token and to final token), throughput (tokens/sec and requests/sec) under steady-state load.
- Cost calc: measured infra cost for run (GPU hours * rate) + model licensing cost (if any) normalized to $/1M generated tokens.

Model configuration & run plan (to include in MAP):
- Redwood-7B-v2-optimized — q4/FP16 baseline; 1-run config: batch_size 8, kv-cache warmup, 2 warmup runs then 10 measured runs.
- Llama-2-13B-chat (int8) — batch_size 4, attention-optimizations enabled; sanity check on hallucination prompts.
- Falcon-40B-instruct (ptq) — single-worker run for quality vs cost tradeoff.

Success criteria (explicit):
- Latency: p95 <= 300ms for 512 tokens (streaming first-token <= 120ms) — this is the hard gate per Aditi's ask.
- Cost: <= $0.00095 per generated token at measured batch settings.
- Quality: >= 90% pass rate on rubric; no critical safety regression.

Infrastructure notes: please include KV cache priming in the run script and capture memory/VRAM utilization per GPU. I added a short checklist row in the MAP for "test harness config" and linked a draft run script (techeval_run.sh) in the Drive folder.

I'll kick off the baseline runs as soon as we get the sample dataset and credentials. Connor — please confirm whether MediSync will permit SSH/VPC peering for a private preview; if not, we'll run in Redwood sandbox and note differences in the readout.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
